message.content: OK, on a fait pas mal de post pour le prochain live, on a pas mal préparé des choses. Là, ce que j'aimerais qu'on vérifie, c'est que tout est opérationnel pour demain, que ça soit d'un point de vue slide et d'un point de vue démo. Voilà, c'est pour finir la prépa pour demain, pour qu'à 14h, j'ai l'esprit libre de ça. Donc, on va recharger les slides. Je vais relire un peu ce qu'on a fait, être sûr que c'est cohérent, mais il me semble qu'on avait déjà fait une passe dessus. et tu vas faire, c'est pas moi qui vais faire, c'est toi qui vas le faire, une passe sur la démo associée et vérifier qu'on mette bien les choses dans l'ordre, on respecte la partie éditoriale, le why, oh, what, on montre bien l'état de départ, on montre bien une erreur, on montre bien le correctif et on a tout ce qu'il faut pour expliquer, le block check, le warning, Moi, j'aimerais bien ajouter aussi un point à cette démo, c'est, il y a par exemple un use case que j'ai en tête, typiquement une clé KMS, dans une clé KMS, on vient rajouter des rôles ou des choses en administrateur dessus, typiquement, je ne sais pas, un rôle DevOps ou un rôle Ops déployé dans le compte, et on peut du coup utiliser le block check pour rajouter de manière conditionnelle ce rôle quand il existe sur un compte, imaginons un cas où il n'existe pas sur tous les environnements. Et du coup, on peut mettre un warning quand il n'existe pas, ou alors simplement le concaténer dans la liste des ARN qui a les droits, dans le cas où il existe.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- handoff: End-of-session handoff. Reconcile the project's tracking file (mark done resolved, promote every leftover to a live item with value+trigger, log decisions/debt/lessons), verify green via the project's oracle command, confirm nothing lives only in chat or a disposable note, persist a disposable resume prompt (with a cold-start reload list of the links that mattered this session) into the tracking file, checkpoint-commit, then compact the note. Project-agnostic. Use when wrapping up, pausing, "prep handoff", "close the session", or "generate a resume prompt".
- linkedin-review: Multi-agent parallel review of a LinkedIn profile against benchmarks, via Playwright MCP browser navigation. Spawns N specialized personas (decideur-client, commercial-esn, personal-branding, concurrent-freelance, copywriter, ats-keywords, seo-linkedin) in parallel, each producing an independent critique. Returns a synthesized report with convergences, conflicts, prioritized actions. Use when the user asks to audit/review their LinkedIn profile.
- review-plan: Multi-agent parallel review of a plan, design doc, or architecture proposal. Spawns N expert personas (product, security, performance, seo, devex, cloud-architecture, finops, compliance, accessibility) in parallel, each producing an independent critique. Returns a synthesized report with convergences, conflicts, and decisions to make. Use when the user asks to review a plan, audit a design, get multiple perspectives on a doc, or run a "multi-agent review".
- rtk: RTK (Rust Token Killer) proxy meta-commands. Use when the user asks for RTK token-savings analytics, command history, missed-opportunity discovery, or wants to bypass the auto-rewrite hook (rtk proxy). The PreToolUse hook auto-rewrites Bash commands transparently - do not invoke this skill for normal commands.
- add-contact: Create one CRM Contact via add-contact.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use when adding a person with optional Org affiliations. For multi-entity free text, use add-lead.
- add-editorial-carousel: Generate a branded LinkedIn carousel (document post) for a piece from the BGA carousel skeleton. Composes N portrait 4:5 pages from the piece narrative (Why/How/What) using page-type primitives (cover, bullets, term, flow, compare, synth, cta - §5.8 catalogue), renders each page for a legibility gate, runs brand-review, delivers a swipeable PDF, wires it back into the piece `## Visuels`. Use when the user wants a carousel, a document post, or a live retex repurposed as swipeable pages.
- add-editorial-idea: Capture a new editorial idea (LinkedIn post, article, talk seed) as an anchor in `02-Areas/Éditorial/Ideas/`. Runs dedup check, applies frontmatter schema, enforces BGA brand conformity, updates MoC. Auto-detects express vs standard mode. Use when the user wants to capture, add, save, or register an editorial idea, post idea, article idea, or content seed.
- add-editorial-piece: Transform an editorial anchor (`Ideas/<file>.md`) into a piece for a given format (linkedin, article, live, podcast, talk). Resolves the anchor, fills frontmatter from template SSoT, drafts the body, runs brand conformity, ticks the matching line in the anchor's Déclinaisons checklist. Use when the user wants to draft a LinkedIn post, article, talk, live, or podcast piece from an existing idea.
- add-editorial-slides: Generate a branded HTML slide deck for a piece from the BGA slides skeleton. Composes slides from the piece narrative (Why/How/What, key points, tables) using slide-type primitives (title, bullets, cards, table, flow, callout, def, compare, probe, layers - §5.7 catalogue) selected per idea via the §5.7 archetype heuristic, renders each slide for a legibility gate, runs brand-review, wires the deck back into the piece. Interactive HTML opened in the browser, no delivery PNG. Use when the user wants intro slides, a live deck, or a talk/workshop deck for an editorial piece.
- add-editorial-visual: Generate a branded editorial visual (square post visual or LinkedIn event banner) for a piece from the BGA HTML skeleton. Reads the piece's `## Visuels` brief (format + disposition + setup/Why + contenu/How + synthèse/What), composes with CSS auto-layout (never hand-placed coordinates), renders HTML->PNG via Playwright, gates on visual legibility + brand-review, wires the asset back into the piece. Use when the user wants a schema, diagram, before/after, lifecycle visual, or event banner for a LinkedIn post, article, or live.
- add-formation: Bootstrap a new BGA formation by aggregating N editorial anchors (`Ideas/*.md`) into a curriculum. Creates the formation folder, generates the index from template, scaffolds one module file per anchor, backlinks each anchor via its Déclinaisons checklist, updates the Formations MoC. Supports direct mode (--ideas arg) or interactive mode (anchor picker grouped by pillar). Use when the user wants to create, scaffold, build, or initialize a training, workshop, masterclass, or curriculum.
- add-interaction: Create one CRM Interaction (dated exchange report) via add-interaction.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use to log a call/meeting/email/event tied to an Opp or Org.
- add-lead: Add a new prospect (Organisation + optional Opportunity + optional Contact) to the CRM. Accepts free text and/or LinkedIn URLs. Use when the user mentions a new company or contact to add.
- add-opportunity: Create one CRM Opportunity via add-opp.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use when adding a new channel/deal on an existing or new target Org. One Opp = one channel.
- add-organisation: Create one CRM Organisation via add-org.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use when adding a single company (no opportunity/contact). For multi-entity free text + LinkedIn, use add-lead.
- archive-opportunity: Move a closed CRM Opportunity (perdu/gagne) to Opportunities/_archive/ via archive-opp.py (git mv, FK-safe). Use to declutter active pipeline after a deal closes.
- archive-project: Guided PARA archival of a finished project. Extracts forward-looking artefacts BEFORE the move - active backlog to Projects, living doc/SSoT to an existing or newly-created Area, structural decisions to ADRs, pure reference to Resources - sets the frozen marker, git mv to 04-Archives, propagates orphan wikilinks. Judgment-heavy (classify + route); writes = git mv + targeted edits. Use when a project is done and must be archived.
- brand-review: Audit a BGA editorial artifact (text and/or visual) against brand SSoT. Verifies tone-of-voice principles, format specs, color tokens, WCAG ratios, text/visual coherence. Outputs a status table + one prioritized recommendation.
- parse-td-results: Parse a Tutorial Dojo HTML exam result, extract incorrect questions, and append summaries to the AWS SAP Mistakes note.
- synthesize-interaction: Synthesize a freelance prospection Interaction draft - restructure the raw note and propagate to the linked Opportunity/Organisation. Thick orchestrator - LLM synthesis only, writes delegated to deterministic scripts.
- update-contact: Update an existing CRM Contact via update-contact.py (deterministic, schema-validated, idempotent). Set personal fields, append Org affiliations or notes.
- update-lead: Quick update of an existing Organisation or Opportunity from free text (informal conversation, phone call, ad-hoc info). Auto-detects the target. Use when the user reports info about an existing prospect.
- update-opportunity: Update an existing CRM Opportunity (non-status fields) via update-opp.py (deterministic, schema-validated, idempotent). For status/lost/won transitions use transition-opp.
- update-organisation: Update an existing CRM Organisation via update-org.py (deterministic, schema-validated, idempotent). Set durable company fields or append to body regions.
- weekly-actions: Display prospection actions for the current calendar week (Mon-Sun), including overdue items. Source - Opportunities. Use when the user asks for actions, planning, or prospection to-do.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

name: BGA editorial - tournure positive par défaut
description: Préférence éditoriale BGA Consulting - formuler en affirmatif, éviter "pas de", "ne plus", "sans", négations multiples. Codifié en principe 2.7 du tone of voice.

Toute production éditoriale BGA Consulting (posts LinkedIn, articles, mails, slides, docs client) doit privilégier les tournures affirmatives. Éviter "pas de X", "ne plus", "sans", négations multiples. Dire ce qu'on fait / protège / rend possible plutôt que ce qu'on évite.

**Why** : marque posée et exigeante, pas alarmiste. Une marque conseil rassure par ce qu'elle construit, pas par ce qu'elle bannit. Le négatif fatigue à la lecture longue et signale une posture défensive. Demande explicite Baptiste 2026-05-10.

**How to apply** :
- Reformuler systématiquement les phrases négatives en affirmatif lors de toute rédaction ou relecture BGA.
- Exception assumée : listes Do/Don't, anti-positions du brief, règles bloquantes (WCAG FAIL, em-dash interdit, etc.) - le négatif y joue un rôle de frontière.
- Codifié dans `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md` section 2.7.
- Lors d'une passe validation sur un texte BGA, traiter ce critère au même titre que les coquilles et le fact-check.

23	# Live - Terraform check : santé post-apply
24	
25	## Accroche

47	> Live technique, démos dans le repo public.
48	> Jeudi 6 août, 13h. LinkedIn + Twitch.

50	> Terraform apply au vert = plateforme qui a convergé, c'est déjà bien.
51	> Et la santé réelle des services déployés alors ?

56	
57	## Corps
58	
59	### Conducteur - Terraform prend le pouls (live S32, jeu. 2026-08-06)
60	
61	Sujet direct (pool ADR-009, décision 2026-08-03) : 3e et dernier volet de l'anchor - query/import joué S25, actions joué S31, `check` referme la trilogie « au-delà du CRUD ». Date engagée à l'antenne au CLOSE du S31 (« jeudi prochain, même heure »). Démo = lab public `examples/terraform-check-health` ([bgauduch/terraform-examples](https://github.com/bgauduch/terraform-examples), PR #29 à rafraîchir et merger sur `main` avant le live : une seule branche à l'écran). Découplage intact : le repo ne référence jamais ce live.
62	
63	Héros : le **bloc `check`** (le mécanisme), pas le site de démo. Scène : terminal + navigateur, micro-deck 4 slides (1er deck sous la règle « 2 slides bloquantes » : teaser + récap+CTA).
64	
65	#### Idée-force : après « agir », « vérifier »
66	
67	Le S31 a fait entrer l'impératif day-2 dans le lifecycle ; ce live fait entrer la **santé réelle** dans le plan. Un `check` porte une **scoped data source relue à chaque plan/apply** + des `assert` ; l'échec est un **warning, jamais un blocage** : signal continu de santé et de drift, sans casser le workflow. Contraste : `precondition`/`postcondition` bloquent, `check` observe.
68	
69	#### Conducteur timé (squelette doctrine, T0 = 13h00, sortie de bloc)
70	
71	| Sortie | Bloc | Support | Objectif + geste |
72	|---|---|---|---|
73	| 13h02 | OPEN | cam | accueil, format, invite chat ; **partage d'écran confirmé au retour programme** |

75	| 13h11 | WHAT teaser (S1) | slide | le couple scoped data source + assert ; warning non-bloquant ; tableau `check` vs `precondition`/`postcondition` ; fact-check : v1.5.0 (juin 2023), GA et sous-coté |
76	| 13h18 | HOW-1 · lab | terminal | visite : site statique S3 + `check "website_health"` (2 asserts : HTTP 200, marqueur `Status: healthy`) ; lecture ligne à ligne ; apply → check vert, site ouvert au navigateur |
77	| 13h26 | HOW-1 · geste | terminal + navigateur | **démo d'échec planifiée** : casser le site dans le dos de Terraform (`aws s3 cp` d'un index falsifié) → `terraform plan` → WARNING drift, exit 0 ; le rouge est le spectacle et il laisse passer |
78	| 13h33 | HOW-2 · déclinaison | terminal | même mécanisme, l'autre versant : `terraform apply` restaure l'objet géré, le check repasse vert - détecter puis réconcilier ; aparté : santé (200) vs drift de contenu (marqueur), un bloc, deux asserts |
79	| 13h38 | LIMITES (S2) | slide | non-bloquant par design (exit 0 : la CI doit lire les warnings) ; évalué au plan/apply seulement en OSS, continuous validation = HCP Terraform ; quand préférer `postcondition` (gate) ou le monitoring réel - le check complète, il remplace rien |
80	| 13h42 | CLOSE (S3) | slide récap+CTA | récap une phrase par bloc + fil « après agir, vérifier » ; CTA affichés : repo, Calendly, one-liner ; teaser : pool de sujets ouvert (date énoncée seulement si sujet arrêté - leçon S31) |

# Live - Terraform check : santé post-apply

## Accroche

**🔬 Description event - v1 générée (2026-08-04, prête à coller depuis l'accroche d'origine) :**

> Live technique, démos réelles dans le repo public. Jeudi 6 août, 13h. LinkedIn + Twitch.
>
> L'apply vert dit que la config a convergé ; la santé réelle du service vit ailleurs. Le bloc check (Terraform 1.5) la ramène dans le plan : assertions sur l'infra déployée, drift détecté à chaque plan/apply, en warning qui laisse le workflow avancer.
>
> On le met à l'épreuve en direct : un site cassé dans le dos de Terraform, et le plan qui le voit.

**✅ Description event - v2 validée Baptiste (2026-08-04, 458 octets - texte brut, prêt à coller dans l'event) :**

> Live technique, démos dans le repo public.
> Jeudi 6 août, 13h. LinkedIn + Twitch.
>
> L'apply vert dit que la config a convergé tandis que la santé réelle du service vit ailleurs.
> Le bloc check (Terraform 1.5) la ramène dans le plan : assertions sur l'infra déployée, drift détecté à chaque plan/apply, en warning qui laisse le workflow avancer.
>
> On le met à l'épreuve en direct : un site cassé dans le dos de Terraform, et le plan qui le détecte.

**✅ Description event - v3 validée Baptiste (2026-08-04, réécriture auteur sur v2 - Why en question incarnée + remédiation nommée ; 2 corrections mécaniques appliquées : « On met la fonctionnalité », « l'épreuve ». 565 octets - texte brut, prêt à coller dans l'event) :**

> Live technique, démos dans le repo public.
> Jeudi 6 août, 13h. LinkedIn + Twitch.
>
> Terraform apply au vert = plateforme qui a convergé, c'est déjà bien.
> Et la santé réelle des services déployés alors ?
>
> Le bloc check (Terraform 1.5) la ramène dans le plan : assertions sur l'infra déployée, drift détecté à chaque plan/apply, en warning qui laisse le workflow avancer.
>
> On met la fonctionnalité à l'épreuve en direct : un site cassé malgré un terraform apply en succès, et le check de remédiation pour détecter l'état de santé dès le plan !

## Corps

### Conducteur - Terraform prend le pouls (live S32, jeu. 2026-08-06)

Sujet direct (pool ADR-009, décision 2026-08-03) : 3e et dernier volet de l'anchor - query/import joué S25, actions joué S31, `check` referme la trilogie « au-delà du CRUD ». Date engagée à l'antenne au CLOSE du S31 (« jeudi prochain, même heure »). Démo = lab public `examples/terraform-check-health` ([bgauduch/terraform-examples](https://github.com/bgauduch/terraform-examples), PR #29 à rafraîchir et merger sur `main` avant le live : une seule branche à l'écran). Découplage intact : le repo ne référence jamais ce live.

Héros : le **bloc `check`** (le mécanisme), pas le site de démo. Scène : terminal + navigateur, micro-deck 4 slides (1er deck sous la règle « 2 slides bloquantes » : teaser + récap+CTA).

#### Idée-force : après « agir », « vérifier »

Le S31 a fait entrer l'impératif day-2 dans le lifecycle ; ce live fait entrer la **santé réelle** dans le plan. Un `check` porte une **scoped data source relue à chaque plan/apply** + des `assert` ; l'échec est un **warning, jamais un blocage** : signal continu de santé et de drift, sans casser le workflow. Contraste : `precondition`/`postcondition` bloquent, `check` observe.

#### Conducteur timé (squelette doctrine, T0 = 13h00, sortie de bloc)

| Sortie | Bloc | Support | Objectif + geste |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13h02 | OPEN | cam | accueil, format, invite chat ; **partage d'écran confirmé au retour programme** |
| 13h08 | WHY (S0) | slide | la trilogie se referme (query S25 · actions S31 · check) ; le trou : apply vert ≠ service sain, le drift ClickOps vit sous le radar entre deux applies ; rappel-outil débutants coupé (renvoi replays) |
| 13h11 | WHAT teaser (S1) | slide | le couple scoped data source + assert ; warning non-bloquant ; tableau `check` vs `precondition`/`postcondition` ; fact-check : v1.5.0 (juin 2023), GA et sous-coté |
| 13h18 | HOW-1 · lab | terminal | visite : site statique S3 + `check "website_health"` (2 asserts : HTTP 200, marqueur `Status: healthy`) ; lecture ligne à ligne ; apply → check vert, site ouvert au navigateur |
| 13h26 | HOW-1 · geste | terminal + navigateur | **démo d'échec planifiée** : casser le site dans le dos de Terraform (`aws s3 cp` d'un index falsifié) → `terraform plan` → WARNING drift, exit 0 ; le rouge est le spectacle et il laisse passer |
| 13h33 | HOW-2 · déclinaison | terminal | même mécanisme, l'autre versant : `terraform apply` restaure l'objet géré, le check repasse vert - détecter puis réconcilier ; aparté : santé (200) vs drift de contenu (marqueur), un bloc, deux asserts |
| 13h38 | LIMITES (S2) | slide | non-bloquant par design (exit 0 : la CI doit lire les warnings) ; évalué au plan/apply seulement en OSS, continuous validation = HCP Terraform ; quand préférer `postcondition` (gate) ou le monitoring réel - le check complète, il remplace rien |
| 13h42 | CLOSE (S3) | slide récap+CTA | récap une phrase par bloc + fil « après agir, vérifier » ; CTA affichés : repo, Calendly, one-liner ; teaser : pool de sujets ouvert (date énoncée seulement si sujet arrêté - leçon S31) |
| ≤14h00 | Q&A optionnelle | cam | amorces : « quel drift vous a déjà mordu ? », « vos checks post-deploy vivent où : script, CI, monitoring ? » |

Coupes par défaut (pied du prompteur) : (1) aparté sécurité du bucket public (`#trivy:ignore` documentés), (2) compresser LIMITES en gardant « quand rester en monitoring ». Beats verrouillés : le tamper, la remédiation, le récap.

- PR #29 rafraîchie (merge `main`, CI verte 15/15), toolchain pin aligné sur la convention mise du repo, squash sur `main`.
- Lab appliqué la veille (site S3 statique : setup instantané, coût négligeable) ; rejouer le tamper + la remédiation ; reset d'état.
- Dry-run timé de la scène finale ; scène modifiée après pré-vol → re-timée.

# CLAUDE.md - Éditorial

Rules for `02-Areas/Éditorial/`. Covers all content brands (BGA + personal).

## Structure

```
Ideas/                       # anchor notes - permanent intellectual asset (type: idee-editoriale)
Pieces/                      # content per format (type: piece)
  Formations/<slug>/         # aggregate format (type: piece-formation)
    index.md
    NN-<module>.md           # module per anchor (type: module-formation)
  Formations/_MoC Formations.md  # index of formations (vs Ideas/_MoC Idées.md for anchors)
Live/                        # live channel doctrine (type: area-doctrine) - lifecycle, stack, diffusion matrix, runbooks
assets/                      # ALL per-piece rendered visuals (ADR-006). Naming <format>-<sujet>.{html,png}, formats in design-system §5.0
ADRs/                        # architecture decision records (MADR-lite, index 00-adr-index.md)
enums.yml                    # executable SSoT of enums (read by lint-editorial.py)
scripts/lint-editorial.py    # linter + auto-fix (template + enums driven)
scripts/transcribe-vod.sh    # live VOD -> filtered transcript (retex source of truth)
Dashboard.md
```

Frontmatter schemas SSoT: `99-Templates/Template - Idee {Editoriale,Express}.md`, `Template - Piece LinkedIn.md`, `Template - Piece.md` (article/live/talk générique), `Template - Piece Formation.md`, `Template - Module Formation.md`. Don't redeclare.

## Idea lifecycle

- **Brute**: bullet line in `Ideas/_MoC Idées.md` §`Idées brutes (#No-Fomo, Bro !)`. Flat, no pillar, no file.
- **Anchor**: file in `Ideas/` with frontmatter. Indexed in MoC under `pillar`. Promote when ≥1 of: angle, source, planned declination.
- **Piece**: file in `Pieces/` per format. Naming: `YYYY-MM-DD <Format> - <Topic>.md` (date = created). Mandatory `idea: "[[anchor]]"` backlink (singleton, 1:1).
- **Publication**: on go-live, set `status: published` + fill `published-date` AND `url` (post/live permalink). Ask the author for the `url` when absent - capture it whenever a published piece is touched, never leave it empty.
- **Piece-formation**: folder in `Pieces/Formations/<slug>/`. `index.md` aggregates N anchors via `ideas: [...]` array. Each module file = 1 anchor (relation 1:1 module → anchor).
- Brutes >30 lines → promotion/archive pass.

## Rules

- **Layer separation** (airtight): branding = design semantics (`../BGA Consulting/Brand/`); editorial structure = forms/sections/enums (`99-Templates/` + this file); content = pieces (`Pieces/`). Never carry one layer into another. E.g. the `## Visuels` brief form is editorial structure (templates); its semantics (disposition recipes, Why/How/What arc, naming) stay branding §5.4; templates delegate by pointer, never restate it.
- Anchor↔Piece: backlink via piece `idea: "[[anchor]]"` only (mandatory on every piece). Schema (target / audience enums) in template SSoT.
- Anchor↔Formation: backlink via formation index `ideas: [...]` array (N:1). Anchor's Déclinaisons checklist tracks the link via `[x] Formation - [[<formation-index>]]`.
- **Live channel** SSoT: [[Doctrine - cycle de vie d'un live]] (`Live/`) - lifecycle, stack, diffusion matrix, TYPE checklists, runbooks.
	- Per-live RUN = the live piece: pre-live cases in `## Notes production`, follow-up in `## Suivi post-live`.
	- Timing/copy rules stay here (§Channel tactics).
- Default capture = brute.
- Pillars SSoT: `../BGA Consulting/Brand/01-Brief.md` §16.
- Evergreen snippets: `../BGA Consulting/Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md`.
- Cross-idea sources: `03-Resources/` wiki-linked from anchors.
- `#to-editorialize` tag on any note → process to brute or anchor, remove tag.
- Déclinaisons block in anchor: edited via `<!-- skill:editorial:declinaisons:start -->` / `:end` HTML anchors only.

## Concision

Applies vault `Note authoring` (root CLAUDE.md §Conventions). Editorial specifics:

- Per-type density quotas live in template headers (SSoT).
- Active voice, short sentences.
- No meta-prose ("in this section we'll...", "it is worth noting...").
- An idea exists in one place; other sections link to it.
- Code blocks: minimal viable, no boilerplate, no explanatory comments when code self-documents.
- Quality signal: if >3 lines can be cut without info loss, it's too long.

## Tooling

Linter SSoT: `scripts/lint-editorial.py` (consolidated, template-aware). Mandatory gate for every write in this area, by skill or by hand.

- Post-write (single file): `python3 02-Areas/Éditorial/scripts/lint-editorial.py --file <path> --apply` then re-run without `--apply` to confirm clean exit.
- Bulk audit: `python3 02-Areas/Éditorial/scripts/lint-editorial.py [--type ideas|pieces] [--apply] [--strict]`.
- Skills that touch ideas / pieces / formations / modules MUST call `--file <path> --apply` before returning, and report residual report-only violations to the user.
- Manual edits: run the same single-file command before commit when frontmatter, tags, headings, anchors, or backlinks were touched.
- Template drift (key absent from `99-Templates/`) → STOP, amend template first, then re-lint.
- Enums externalized: `enums.yml` (executable SSoT, hand-parsed, zero-dep). Linter reads it at runtime. See Data model & couplages for sync rules.

Visual generation: skill `add-editorial-visual` produces a piece's branded visual from its `## Visuels` brief (`format` + intention; `disposition` for square). Format dispatch, skeletons (`skeletons/<format>.html`), dims, naming, output home: design-system §5.0 registry. Render HTML->PNG via `../BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/render-html.mjs`; brand-review gate. ADR-006: all per-piece renders in `assets/`, never in `Brand/`.

Slides generation: skill `add-editorial-slides` produces a piece's branded HTML deck (slide-types per design-system §5.7, skeleton `skeletons/slides.html`), composed from the piece narrative. Legibility gate per slide (`?slide=N` via `render-html.mjs`) + brand-review; output `assets/slides-<sujet>.html` (interactive HTML, delivered as-is, no PNG). Wired into the piece `## Notes production` (live-support artifact), not `## Visuels`.

Carousel generation: LinkedIn document post (design-system §5.8, ADR-007), skeleton `../BGA Consulting/Brand/skeletons/carousel.html`. N pages portrait 4:5, composed from a piece (typically a live retex). Legibility gate per page (`?page=N`) + brand-review; **delivery PDF** via `_pipeline/render-pdf.mjs`; output `assets/carousel-<sujet>.{html,pdf}` (per-page PNG transient, not persisted). `carousel` is in the `visual-format` enum (it IS a `linkedin` piece's `## Visuels`, unlike slides). Generated by skill `add-editorial-carousel` (skeleton + per-page legibility gate + brand-review + PDF delivery + wire into `## Visuels` + lint), same filière as `add-editorial-slides`/`add-editorial-visual`; hand-craft from the skeleton stays possible.

## Data model & coupling

Home of the editorial data model (no separate `Modèle de données.md` - CRM lesson ADR-019). Structuring decisions: `ADRs/` (MADR-lite, index `ADRs/00-adr-index.md`); project context: sub-project `Gouvernance données éditoriales`.

Entities: `idee-editoriale` (anchor) · `piece` (per format) · `piece-formation` (index) · `module-formation` · asset (file in `assets/`).
Relations: anchor 1→N piece (FK `piece.idea`) · anchor N→1 formation (`formation.ideas[]`) · module 1:1 anchor (`module.idea`) · piece →N asset (body wikilink; `assets[]` frontmatter deferred) · piece →N lead→CRM (cross-area).

Coupling (who owns what, who reads, sync mode):

| Artifact                                                                                                                                   | SSoT of                                                                                                            | Read by                                                                | Sync                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `99-Templates/Template - *.md`                                                                                                             | frontmatter keys, headings, defaults                                                                               | `lint-editorial.py` (runtime)                                          | **auto** - the linter reads the template at runtime; changing a key CANNOT desync the linter                             |
| `enums.yml`                                                                                                                                | enum values (pillar/brand/format/status/target/audience) + legacy-tags + canonical-formats                         | `lint-editorial.py` (runtime)                                          | **auto** on the linter side                                                                                              |
| `enums.yml` ↔ human SSoTs: `../BGA Consulting/Brand/01-Brief.md §16` (pillar/target), root CLAUDE.md (format→template), templates (status) | business values                                                                                                    | human                                                                  | **MANUAL** - propagate on both sides, same commit                                                                        |
| `../BGA Consulting/Brand/03-Design-system.md §5.0` (registry) + §5.4/5.6 (specs)                                                           | `## Visuels` brief semantics, visual-format registry (format→dims/§/skeleton/naming/home), per-format design specs | templates (pointer), `add-editorial-visual`, `brand-review`            | **MANUAL** doc-to-doc                                                                                                    |
| asset naming `<format>-<subject>.{html,png}` (registry §5.0, ADR-006)                                                                      | §5.0                                                                                                               | `lint-editorial.py` (`ASSET_REF_RE`, extension-based, prefix-agnostic) | **MANUAL** - changing the extension → update §5.0 + linter regex; the format prefix is convention-only (no regex impact) |

Enums: values **in English**, **centralized in `enums.yml`** (ADR-005, keys + values). Templates and skills **point** to `enums.yml`, never restate values (so no template/skill ↔ enums drift). `visual-format` (square/event-banner) in `enums.yml`, format specs in design-system §5.0 registry; `disposition` (visual enum) points to §5.4. Reference to `enums.yml` = backticked path, never wikilink (non-note file).

Anti-drift rule: before touching a template, an enum, or asset naming, read the Sync column. **auto** coupling (keys/headings/enums read at runtime) cannot drift by construction. **MANUAL** coupling must be propagated in the same commit. The classic "template changes a field, linter out of date" = **auto** for keys (impossible); the real risk is enum value ↔ human doc and asset naming ↔ regex.

## Brand

- `brand: bga` - apply `../BGA Consulting/Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md` (positive phrasing, anti-positions, brand adjectives).
- `brand: personal` - free tone.
- **Copy corpus**: author-corrected copy keeps both versions in the piece.
	- `linkedin` → `## Version publication` · `live` → `🔬 Copy` block in `## Notes production`.
	- Typed delta logged in `../BGA Consulting/Brand/Corpus copy - généré vs validé.md` (3 occurrences → voice rule).

## Channel tactics

Channel-specific publication rules. Volatile (platform algorithms) - date each rule, revise on signal. `format` frontmatter = channel SSoT; pieces stay flat in `Pieces/` (folder only for inherently multi-file artifacts, e.g. `Pieces/Formations/`). Promote a channel to `Channels/<name>.md` only if its ruleset outgrows ~10 lines.

### LinkedIn

- Hashtags (rev. 2026-05-29): 3-5 max (>5 = reach penalty), 1 broad + niche, PascalCase, bottom of post, aligned to copy keywords. Marginal effect (passive SEO), not a reach lever. Tailor per topic, don't reuse one set. Re-validate if distribution shifts. Source: cross-research Sprout Social / ContentIn / ConnectSafely.
- Body: hook line 1 ≤220c (fold), standalone, no rhetorical-question opener (brand §4.1). External links → first comment, never in body. Code/identifiers as plain indented text (LinkedIn strips monospace).
- CTA discret (brand §4.1); omit for pure-technical posts.
- Visual: `square` format (SSoT design-system §5.0 registry + §5.4 spec, tokens + WCAG §1). Generated by skill `add-editorial-visual` (skeleton + brand-review gate), not by hand.
- Cadence: 1 post / 2 semaines (cf `Dashboard.md`).
- **Timing** (rev. 2026-07-07, priors best-practice B2B FR tech - **à recalibrer sur les analytics des posts**) : jours **mar/mer/jeu** (mardi + jeudi les plus forts en B2B ; lundi = bruit, ven après-midi + week-end = creux). Créneaux par ordre de reach : **matin 07h45-09h00** (prime, viser ~08h00), **déjeuner 12h-13h** (secondaire), **soir 17h30-19h** (tertiaire, mode détente). Poster **~15 min avant le pic** (golden hour : l'algo pondère l'engagement des 60-90 premières min). **1er commentaire (liens) posté dans la foulée** ; répondre aux premiers commentaires dans l'heure. **1 post / jour max** par profil (évite l'auto-cannibalisation). Programmation via le scheduler LinkedIn natif. Créneau retenu tracé à la programmation : pièce `live` → `## Notes production` ; pièce `linkedin` (pas de `## Notes production` au template) → tracking du projet/cadence porteur.
- **Rythme de promo d'un live** : annonce à runway (J-2/J-1, ou soir J-3 pour maximiser le save-the-date) + **relance jour-J ~08h** + **nudge ~12h50** (« on est live ») ; le live occupe le créneau déj. Un retex (carrousel) est evergreen → peut viser un prime slot standalone même décalé.
- **Promo d'un event/live (mécanique LinkedIn, rev. 2026-07-07)** : pour l'annonce, privilégier le **partage de l'event** (copy courte au-dessus) à un post texte + lien. La carte event est **cliquable → inscription directe + rappels auto**, et **native** (pas de pénalité « lien externe ») ; garder le 1er commentaire pour les liens externes (Calendly/repo). Le live génère un **post auto au démarrage** (copy générique, instant T) → l'annonce sert l'anticipation/l'inscription, un autre moment du funnel, donc pas redondante.

### Sondage choix de sujet (live)

Sondage LinkedIn faisant voter le sujet du prochain live. Règle (SSoT ADR-009) :
- Chaque option = item de backlog **ancré avant publication** (anchor `Ideas/` si riche, sinon brute dans `_MoC Idées.md`) ; le corps **wikilinke** chaque option vers son foyer.
- Pièce `format: linkedin` **taggée `sondage`**, filée comme tout post (via `add-editorial-piece`, gate linter).
- `idea:` (FK 1:1) pointe l'anchor **gagnant** ; multi-sujets → autres options cross-linkées dans le corps ; sondage ouvert → `idea:` provisoire, repointé sur le gagnant à la clôture.
- À la clôture : gagnant → `piece` `live` ; **options non retenues restent ancrées** (anchor `[ ] Live` ouvert, ou brute annotée `(sondage S<N>, non retenu)`) = pool réutilisable. Visibilité : Dashboard `## Sondages`.

=========== README.md # terraform-check-health > **Type**: `lab` > **Tags**: `aws` `check` `drift` `post-apply` `v1.5` Terraform **1.5** introduced **`check` blocks**: assertions about your **real, deployed** infrastructure that run on `plan` and `apply` and report failures as **warnings, not errors** - so they never block your workflow. This lab uses one to verify a live website is healthy and to **catch out-of-band drift** on the next plan. ## The idea A `check` block can own a **scoped data source** (re-read every run) and one or more `assert`s: ```hcl check "website_health" { data "http" "home" { url = "http://${aws_s3_bucket_website_configuration.site.website_endpoint}" } assert { condition = data.http.home.status_code == 200 error_message = "Website returned HTTP ${data.http.home.status_code}, expected 200." } assert { condition = strcontains(data.http.home.response_body, "Status: healthy") error_message = "Website body is missing the expected marker - content drift." } } ``` ## `check` vs `precondition` / `postcondition` | | When it runs | On failure | |---|---|---| | `precondition` / `postcondition` | during a resource's plan/apply | **errors** - blocks the apply | | `check` | after resources, on every plan/apply | **warns** - never blocks | Use `check` for continuous health and drift signals you do *not* want to halt a deployment. ## What gets deployed - A public S3 **static website** (instant, no CDN) serving `content/index.html`. - One `check` asserting the endpoint returns **200** and serves the expected content. ## Security baseline A static-website bucket is **public by design**. ACL-based public access stays blocked; the two policy-related public-access guards are intentionally relaxed and documented with `#trivy:ignore` lines (`AVD-AWS-0093`, `AVD-AWS-0087`), plus `AVD-AWS-0132` (SSE-S3 is fine for public content). ## Prerequisites - **Terraform `>= 1.5.0`** (pinned via `mise.toml`; `check` blocks do not exist before 1.5). - AWS provider `~> 5.0` (contemporary with the 1.5 floor) + `http` provider. - AWS credentials for `apply` (`validate`/`plan` need none). Default region: `eu-west-1`. ## Run (live demo) ```bash terraform init terraform apply # deploys the site; the check runs and passes (green). terraform output website_url # open it -> "Status: healthy" ``` Now simulate **out-of-band drift** and watch the check warn (without blocking): ```bash # Break the live site behind Terraform's back - replace the object via the AWS CLI: echo '

That is what makes checks safe > for continuous drift detection in CI or on a schedule. `terraform validate` (CI) does not execute > the data source, so it needs no credentials. =========== main.tf locals { index_html = "${path.module}/content/index.html" common_tags = { Project = var.project ManagedBy = "terraform" } } resource "random_id" "suffix" { byte_length = 4 } # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # A public S3 static website. It is intentionally public so the check block can # assert it over plain HTTP - see the README "Security baseline" section. # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- resource "aws_s3_bucket" "site" { bucket = "${var.project}-${random_id.suffix.hex}" tags = local.common_tags } # A static-website bucket is public by design, so the policy-related public-access # guards are intentionally relaxed (ACL-based public access stays blocked). These # two findings are the cost of a public website and are documented, not hidden. #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0093 #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0087 resource "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block" "site" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.site.id block_public_acls = true block_public_policy = false ignore_public_acls = true restrict_public_buckets = false } resource "aws_s3_bucket_website_configuration" "site" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.site.id index_document { suffix = "index.html" } } resource "aws_s3_bucket_versioning" "site" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.site.id versioning_configuration { status = "Enabled" } } # SSE-S3 (AES256) is fine for a public static website; a customer-managed KMS key # (AVD-AWS-0132) adds no value for content that is served publicly anyway. #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0132 resource "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration" "site" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.site.id rule { apply_server_side_encryption_by_default { sse_algorithm = "AES256" } } } # Public read of objects - this is the whole point of a static website bucket. data "aws_iam_policy_document" "public_read" { statement { sid = "PublicRead" actions = ["s3:GetObject"] resources = ["${aws_s3_bucket.site.arn}/*"] principals { type = "*" identifiers = ["*"] } } } resource "aws_s3_bucket_policy" "site" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.site.id policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.public_read.json depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.site] } resource "aws_s3_object" "index" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.site.id key = "index.html" source = local.index_html etag = filemd5(local.index_html) content_type = "text/html" } # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # check blocks (Terraform 1.5+): post-apply assertions on the REAL deployed # infrastructure. They run on plan and apply, and report FAILURES as warnings - # they never block the workflow. The scoped data source is re-read every run, so # out-of-band drift is caught on the next plan. # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- check "website_health" { data "http" "home" { url = "http://${aws_s3_bucket_website_configuration.site.website_endpoint}" } assert { condition = data.http.home.status_code == 200 error_message = "Website returned HTTP ${data.http.home.status_code}, expected 200 (is the site up?)." } assert { condition = strcontains(data.http.home.response_body, "Status: healthy") error_message = "Website body is missing the expected marker - content drift or a broken deploy." } } =========== variables.tf variable "region" { description = "AWS region" type = string default = "eu-west-1" validation { condition = can(regex("^[a-z]{2}-[a-z]+-[0-9]$", var.region)) error_message = "region must be a valid AWS region identifier, e.g. eu-west-1." } nullable = false } variable "project" { description = "Project name used for the bucket name and tagging" type = string default = "demo-tf-check" validation { condition = can(regex("^[a-z0-9-]{3,40}$", var.project)) error_message = "project must be 3-40 chars, lowercase letters, digits or hyphens (used as an S3 bucket prefix)." } nullable = false } =========== outputs.tf output "website_url" { description = "HTTP URL of the S3 static website (the endpoint asserted by the check)" value = "http://${aws_s3_bucket_website_configuration.site.website_endpoint}" } output "bucket_name" { description = "Name of the website bucket" value = aws_s3_bucket.site.id } =========== providers.tf terraform { # `check` blocks are available since Terraform 1.5. The AWS provider is pinned # to the 5.x line, which is contemporary with the 1.5 floor this example targets. required_version = ">= 1.5.0" required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "~> 5.0" } http = { source = "hashicorp/http" version = "~> 3.0" } random = { source = "hashicorp/random" version = "~> 3.0" } } backend "local" { path = "terraform.tfstate" } } provider "aws" { region = var.region } =========== mise.toml # Terraform pin for this example: 1.5 is the minimum version that ships the `check` block. # tflint/trivy are inherited from the repo-root mise.toml. =========== AGENTS.md # AGENTS.md - terraform-check-health example Guidance for AI coding agents working inside this example. Repo-wide conventions live in the root `AGENTS.md`; this file covers what is specific to `terraform-check-health`. Taxonomy: **type `lab`** - progressive, playable in a live session. Tags: `aws`, `check`, `drift`, `post-apply`, `v1.5`. ## Purpose and scope A **pedagogical demo** (live tech session, 25-30 min). It illustrates Terraform 1.5 `check` blocks: post-apply assertions on the **real** deployed website, and out-of-band **drift detection** that surfaces as a non-blocking warning on the next `plan`. Keep it minimal and fast (a public S3 website, no CDN) so the apply → break → plan-warns → fix loop fits a short live slot. Do not turn the `check` into a `precondition`/`postcondition`: the lesson is that checks **warn** instead of blocking. ## Architecture Single root module (`providers.tf` is auto-discovered by CI): - Public S3 static website (`aws_s3_bucket` + website config + public-read policy) serving `content/index.html`. - One `check "website_health"` with a scoped `data "http"` and two `assert`s (status 200 + body marker). The data source is re-read on every plan/apply, which is what catches drift. ## Common commands ```bash terraform init terraform apply # check runs, passes # tamper with the live object via the AWS CLI (see README), then: terraform plan # check emits a WARNING, exit code stays 0 terraform apply # restores managed content, check green again terraform destroy ``` Validation before committing: `terraform fmt -recursive` (root) and `terraform validate` here. `validate` does not execute the `http` data source, so it needs no network/credentials. ## Prerequisites - Terraform `>= 1.5.0` (pinned in `.terraform-version`; `check` and `strcontains` both land in 1.5). - AWS provider `~> 5.0` + `http` provider; AWS credentials for `apply`. Default region `eu-west-1`. ## Conventions in this example - The bucket is intentionally public; keep ACL public-access blocked and document the two relaxed policy guards with `#trivy:ignore` (`AVD-AWS-0093`, `AVD-AWS-0087`) - do not silence silently. - Assertions reference the scoped `data.http.home`; keep the data source inside the `check` block so it is re-read each run (drift detection depends on this). - Tags via `local.common_tags` (`Project` / `ManagedBy`).

These # two findings are the cost of a public website and are documented, not hidden. #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0093 #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0087 resource "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block" "site" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.site.id block_public_acls = true block_public_policy = false ignore_public_acls = true restrict_public_buckets = false } resource "aws_s3_bucket_website_configuration" "site" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.site.id index_document { suffix = "index.html" } } resource "aws_s3_bucket_versioning" "site" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.site.id versioning_configuration { status = "Enabled" } } # SSE-S3 (AES256) is fine for a public static website; a customer-managed KMS key # (AVD-AWS-0132) adds no value for content that is served publicly anyway. #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0132 resource "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration" "site" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.site.id rule { apply_server_side_encryption_by_default { sse_algorithm = "AES256" } } } # Public read of objects - this is the whole point of a static website bucket. data "aws_iam_policy_document" "public_read" { statement { sid = "PublicRead" actions = ["s3:GetObject"] resources = ["${aws_s3_bucket.site.arn}/*"] principals { type = "*" identifiers = ["*"] } } } resource "aws_s3_bucket_policy" "site" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.site.id policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.public_read.json depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.site] } resource "aws_s3_object" "index" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.site.id key = "index.html" source = local.index_html etag = filemd5(local.index_html) content_type = "text/html" } # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # check blocks (Terraform 1.5+): post-apply assertions on the REAL deployed # infrastructure. They run on plan and apply, and report FAILURES as warnings - # they never block the workflow. The scoped data source is re-read every run, so # out-of-band drift is caught on the next plan. # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- check "website_health" { data "http" "home" { url = "http://${aws_s3_bucket_website_configuration.site.website_endpoint}" } assert { condition = data.http.home.status_code == 200 error_message = "Website returned HTTP ${data.http.home.status_code}, expected 200 (is the site up?)." } assert { condition = strcontains(data.http.home.response_body, "Status: healthy") error_message = "Website body is missing the expected marker - content drift or a broken deploy." } } =========== variables.tf variable "region" { description = "AWS region" type = string default = "eu-west-1" validation { condition = can(regex("^[a-z]{2}-[a-z]+-[0-9]$", var.region)) error_message = "region must be a valid AWS region identifier, e.g. eu-west-1." } nullable = false } variable "project" { description = "Project name used for the bucket name and tagging" type = string default = "demo-tf-check" validation { condition = can(regex("^[a-z0-9-]{3,40}$", var.project)) error_message = "project must be 3-40 chars, lowercase letters, digits or hyphens (used as an S3 bucket prefix)." } nullable = false } =========== outputs.tf output "website_url" { description = "HTTP URL of the S3 static website (the endpoint asserted by the check)" value = "http://${aws_s3_bucket_website_configuration.site.website_endpoint}" } output "bucket_name" { description = "Name of the website bucket" value = aws_s3_bucket.site.id } =========== providers.tf terraform { # `check` blocks are available since Terraform 1.5. The AWS provider is pinned # to the 5.x line, which is contemporary with the 1.5 floor this example targets. required_version = ">= 1.5.0" required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "~> 5.0" } http = { source = "hashicorp/http" version = "~> 3.0" } random = { source = "hashicorp/random" version = "~> 3.0" } } backend "local" { path = "terraform.tfstate" } } provider "aws" { region = var.region } =========== mise.toml # Terraform pin for this example: 1.5 is the minimum version that ships the `check` block. # tflint/trivy are inherited from the repo-root mise.toml. [tools] terraform = "1.5.0" =========== content/index.html Terraform check demo

=========== AGENTS.md # AGENTS.md - terraform-check-health example Guidance for AI coding agents working inside this example. Repo-wide conventions live in the root `AGENTS.md`; this file covers what is specific to `terraform-check-health`. Taxonomy: **type `lab`** - progressive, playable in a live session. Tags: `aws`, `check`, `drift`, `post-apply`, `v1.5`. ## Purpose and scope A **pedagogical demo** (live tech session, 25-30 min). It illustrates Terraform 1.5 `check` blocks: post-apply assertions on the **real** deployed website, and out-of-band **drift detection** that surfaces as a non-blocking warning on the next `plan`. Keep it minimal and fast (a public S3 website, no CDN) so the apply → break → plan-warns → fix loop fits a short live slot. Do not turn the `check` into a `precondition`/`postcondition`: the lesson is that checks **warn** instead of blocking. ## Architecture Single root module (`providers.tf` is auto-discovered by CI): - Public S3 static website (`aws_s3_bucket` + website config + public-read policy) serving `content/index.html`. - One `check "website_health"` with a scoped `data "http"` and two `assert`s (status 200 + body marker). The data source is re-read on every plan/apply, which is what catches drift. ## Common commands ```bash terraform init terraform apply # check runs, passes # tamper with the live object via the AWS CLI (see README), then: terraform plan # check emits a WARNING, exit code stays 0 terraform apply # restores managed content, check green again terraform destroy ``` Validation before committing: `terraform fmt -recursive` (root) and `terraform validate` here. `validate` does not execute the `http` data source, so it needs no network/credentials. ## Prerequisites - Terraform `>= 1.5.0` (pinned in `.terraform-version`; `check` and `strcontains` both land in 1.5). - AWS provider `~> 5.0` + `http` provider; AWS credentials for `apply`. Default region `eu-west-1`. ## Conventions in this example - The bucket is intentionally public; keep ACL public-access blocked and document the two relaxed policy guards with `#trivy:ignore` (`AVD-AWS-0093`, `AVD-AWS-0087`) - do not silence silently. - Assertions reference the scoped `data.http.home`; keep the data source inside the `check` block so it is re-read each run (drift detection depends on this). - Tags via `local.common_tags` (`Project` / `ManagedBy`).

content.content:
name: Terraform quality

on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: terraform-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  discover:
    name: Discover Terraform root modules
    # Always run on push; on pull_request, run only for fork PRs
    # (same-repo PRs are already covered by the push event).
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      cells: ${{ steps.find.outputs.cells }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3
      - id: find
        # Any directory under examples/ containing providers.tf is a root module to validate.
        # name = path minus examples/ ; example = examples/<name> (holds the per-example tooling).
        run: |
          cells=$(find examples -name providers.tf -printf '%h\n' | sort \
            | jq -R -s '
                split("\n")
                | map(select(length > 0))
                | map({
                    dir: .,
                    name: (sub("^examples/"; "")),
                    example: (split("/")[0:2] | join("/"))
                  })')
          echo "cells=$(echo "$cells" | jq -c .)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  fmt:
    name: terraform fmt
    needs: discover
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3
      - uses: ./.github/actions/tf-setup
      - run: terraform fmt -check -recursive -diff

  quality:
    name: validate + lint + scan (${{ matrix.cell.name }})
    needs: discover
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        cell: ${{ fromJSON(needs.discover.outputs.cells) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3

      - uses: ./.github/actions/tf-setup
        with:
          working-directory: ${{ matrix.cell.dir }}

      - name: terraform init (no backend)
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.cell.dir }}
        run: terraform init -backend=false -input=false

      - name: terraform validate
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.cell.dir }}
        run: terraform validate -no-color

      - name: tflint init
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.cell.dir }}
        run: tflint --init --config "${{ github.workspace }}/${{ matrix.cell.example }}/.tflint.hcl"
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: tflint
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.cell.dir }}
        run: tflint --recursive --format compact --config "${{ github.workspace }}/${{ matrix.cell.example }}/.tflint.hcl"

      # trivy is installed by tf-setup (mise.toml) - no separate setup step.
      - name: trivy config scan (report + gate)
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.cell.dir }}
        run: |
          # Scan once to JSON, then convert the same results twice:
          #   - report: MEDIUM,HIGH,CRITICAL, never fails the job (visibility).
          #   - gate:   HIGH,CRITICAL, fails the job (exit-code 1) if any are found.
          trivy config . --format json --output trivy.json --exit-code 0

          echo "::group::Trivy findings (MEDIUM,HIGH,CRITICAL - report only)"
          trivy convert --format table --severity MEDIUM,HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 0 trivy.json
          echo "::endgroup::"

          trivy convert --format table --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 1 trivy.json
